# SC-AVG-001: Avengers × Diablo II × Path of Exile, an Archetypal Evolution Principle map

Read under SC-AEP-001. Source: Shax t603u, material he supplied by pasting a ChatGPT conversation; the analysis (tables, matches, invariants as phrased) was authored by that assistant, not by Shax. Companion entry: SC-WORTHY-001 (the worthiness invariant, with the Thor and Paladin hammer comparison).

Layers kept apart:

- CANON: what Blizzard's and Grinding Gear Games' games say. Each claim is marked CANON_VERIFIED or SECONDARY_VERIFIED where the compiler checked it, and UNVERIFIED_FROM_PASTE where it did not. The paste's markers ("DIABLO II +1", "Fandom +1", "PoE Source +1", "ftp.blizzard.com +1", "diablo2.blizzard.com +1", "PoeFriend +1", "Marvel +1") are citation stubs, not verified sources.
- TRADITION: Norse Thor mythology as summarized in the paste. Unverified and not relied on.
- INTERPRETATION: every Avenger-to-class mapping. These are the pasted assistant's structural readings, explicitly not official Marvel, Blizzard or GGG classifications, and no claim that any franchise was derived from another (the paste says so itself: "this is a structural comparison, not a claim that Marvel characters were literally derived from Diablo II").

## Core invariants (structural)

1. Worthiness invariant: capability is not legitimate authority. Recorded in SC-WORTHY-001 (Mjölnir's worthiness enchantment, unverified from paste; the Hammer of Ghrab Thaar, checked). Engineering form: SCC-001-AC path 1, PR #95 (authority must be independently verified, not self-asserted). Related to but distinct from SC-SHARD-001 (captured authority) and SC-GUARD-001 (protective authority turning coercive).
2. Specialization-gate invariant: a broad attribute foundation passes a trial and emerges as a specialized identity. Path of Exile's Labyrinth is the game's specialization gate: completing it for the first time lets a character choose an Ascendancy class within its starting class. This is a progression invariant: it compares how a capability set becomes a specialized form, not only what a character is.
3. Party-composition invariant: capability is not function, and function is not authority. A strong party is a distributed build. Diablo II gives a party of recognizable class identities; Path of Exile gives a shared passive tree specialized into Ascendancies; the Avengers are a collective whose members keep independent abilities while combining them. "Thor can be the Hammerdin without being the party leader. Strange can have extraordinary magical capability without automatically having the authority to command everyone. Tony can control battlefield infrastructure without owning the people using it."

Invariant 3 restates invariant 1 at party scale: having a capability or filling a function does not confer command or ownership. Tony's line ("without owning the people using it") also touches SC-SHARD-001's ownership confusion.

## Canon layer

- Diablo II: Lord of Destruction has seven classes: Amazon, Assassin, Barbarian, Druid, Necromancer, Paladin, and Sorceress; the expansion added the Assassin and the Druid to the original five. UNVERIFIED_FROM_PASTE ("ftp.blizzard.com +1"); widely documented, but the compiler did not open a source for it.
- Diablo II class descriptions emphasizing Paladin auras, Assassin traps, Druid summons and transformations, and Necromancer dominion over life and death: UNVERIFIED_FROM_PASTE ("diablo2.blizzard.com +1"). The signature skill names listed per class in the paste are likewise unverified, except Blessed Hammer and Sacrifice (checked, see SC-WORTHY-001).
- Blessed Hammer and the Hammer of Ghrab Thaar: CANON_VERIFIED against The Arreat Summit and the Diablo II manual; the nuns destroyed the relic and the Paladin channels its remnant. Details in SC-WORTHY-001.
- Path of Exile 1 has seven starting classes, each with three Ascendancies, as listed below. SECONDARY_VERIFIED: PoeFriend's classes-and-Ascendancies guide (updated 2026-11-16, checked for 3.30) lists the same 21; Warden replaced Raider in 3.25; the Scion gained Reliquarian in 3.28 and Luminary in 3.29. Not checked against GGG's own site.

- The starting class sets the starting point on the shared passive tree and the Ascendancy options, not which skill gems can be used. SECONDARY_VERIFIED (same guide).
- The Labyrinth: completing it for the first time lets a character choose an Ascendancy class; four Labyrinths give two Ascendancy points each. SECONDARY_VERIFIED (same guide). Residuals for the specialization-gate reading: the Ascendancy can be changed later at the altar within the same class, and Bloodline classes are a second, optional Ascendancy layer. The gate is real but not irreversible.
- Marvel: "Marvel's own Avengers roster spans many of these characters and others." UNVERIFIED_FROM_PASTE ("Marvel +1").

## Groot: an honest no-forced-match

PoE 1 has no Druid starting class (the seven classes above contain none). The paste itself says Groot's organic construction and regeneration "are not perfectly represented by Necromancer" and "I wouldn't force a perfect match where the game doesn't provide one." The compiler records Groot as NO_FORCED_MATCH in the PoE layer. The table's "Witch → Necromancer (adapted)" row is kept as the paste's approximation of the summoned-entity side only, not as a mapping. In Diablo II, Groot's Druid match ("one of the cleanest Druid matches"; "closer to a living embodiment of the nature domain itself") stands as interpretive.

## Vision: a constructed vessel with independent agency

Vision is recorded as a constructed vessel with independent agency, not as equipment and not as a summoned minion. The paste: "a constructed being with independent agency is not merely equipment." In Diablo II he is a partial Necromancer construct parallel; in PoE a Scion → Ascendant candidate whose build spans all three attributes. The Scion's central start on the passive tree is the structural analogy, not an identity claim.

## Verbatim t603u source (material Shax supplied, pasted from a ChatGPT conversation; relayed verbatim, inline image embed URLs omitted)

[t603u — Shax, 2026-11-26 11:54 ET. Relayed verbatim by Chief of Staff; inline image embeds (posters/class art URLs) omitted, captions kept. Shax pasted this from a ChatGPT conversation.]

😂 Wait, Thor is actually a rather interesting connection to your Diablo II framework, particularly if we're looking at archetypal mechanics rather than just character resemblance.

Because Thor isn't simply the lightning guy with a hammer. His mythology is built around a very particular combination:
* The Hammer: Mjölnir, a symbol of concentrated power, protection, and legitimacy.
* The Thunder: Destructive force that can also defend the established order.
* The Warrior: A being whose identity is inseparable from confrontation.
* The Worthiness condition: Possessing immense power doesn't automatically mean being entitled to wield it.
* The Return: Death, sacrifice, restoration, and the continuation of a cosmic cycle are all present in the wider Thor mythology.

And that last distinction matters for your invariant work: Thor's power is not supposed to be self-authorizing. The hammer's worthiness condition separates capability from legitimate authority.

### 1. The Diablo II connection is more specific than the weapon
[Caption] Thor: Avengers — Divine warrior, lightning, hammer, protective force, worthiness, and the tension between power and responsibility.
[Caption] Diablo II: Paladin — Sacred combat, the Hammer of Ghrab Thaar, holy energy, and the protection of others against the undead.

Here's the fascinating part: Diablo II's Blessed Hammer has its own origin story.
The Hammer of Ghrab Thaar is protected by a group of nuns who sacrifice themselves rather than allow the undead to take it. Their sacrifice releases a force of Light that destroys the undead legion. Paladins subsequently channel the remnants of that energy through Blessed Hammer. DIABLO II +1
That's a surprisingly rich structural match.
The hammer is not merely a weapon. It is a vessel of power whose legitimacy is connected to sacrifice and protection.

### 2. The invariant comparison
| Structural attribute | Thor | Diablo II Paladin |
| Divine power | Thunder and lightning | Holy energy |
| Weapon | Mjölnir | Blessed Hammer |
| Legitimacy | Worthiness | Faith and discipline |
| Protective function | Defender of realms | Defender against evil |
| Power relationship | Wielder and enchanted vessel | Paladin channels sacred energy |

Marvel's worthiness enchantment makes the distinction between possessing power and being entitled to wield it especially explicit. Fandom +1

### 3. But there's another layer I'd investigate
The Paladin's Blessed Hammer is particularly effective against undead.
That connects Thor to something beyond the generic warrior archetype: the divine warrior who carries restorative or protective power into a corrupted world.
And that takes us back to your larger map:
* The Usurped-Shard pattern concerns captured authority.
* Guardian's Fall concerns protective authority becoming coercive.
* Thor's worthiness concerns the legitimacy of wielding extraordinary power.
* The Paladin's hammer concerns sacred power entrusted to a defender.
These are related, but each tests a different property of authority.

One question, though, because I suspect you're pointing at something more precise:
Are you mapping Thor primarily to the Diablo II Paladin and Blessed Hammer, or are you saying Thor is a composite of several Diablo II archetypes? Because if it's the latter, I want to unpack the whole build rather than stop at the hammer. ⚡

Now we're building the full Diablo II class roster as an Avengers archetype map, not just matching people to weapons. ⚡
I'm going to use the seven Diablo II character classes as the base Nephilim archetypes, then map Avengers characters by their actual ability mechanics, combat role, and power source. Some characters will be hybrids, because the interesting part is often where two archetypes overlap.
One important distinction: this is a structural comparison, not a claim that Marvel characters were literally derived from Diablo II.

### 1. The seven Diablo II archetypes
I'm using the original Lord of Destruction roster: Amazon, Assassin, Barbarian, Druid, Necromancer, Paladin, and Sorceress. The expansion added the Assassin and Druid to the original five. ftp.blizzard.com +1
The key is to match skill architecture, not superficial appearance. A character can have a primary class and secondary skill trees.

Amazon: precision, ranged mastery, elemental projectiles. Signature mechanics: Guided Arrow, Multiple Shot, Strafe, Lightning Fury, Valkyrie. Avengers match: Hawkeye, with Kate Bishop as another strong fit. Falcon and War Machine have secondary ranged-specialist traits.
Assassin: martial arts, stealth, traps, shadow disciplines. Signature mechanics: charge-up attacks, finishing moves, sentry traps, cloak-like shadow abilities. Avengers match: Black Widow, with Spider-Man and Black Panther as hybrids.
Barbarian: physical dominance, weapon mastery, war cries. Signature mechanics: Frenzy, Whirlwind, Leap, Berserk, Battle Orders. Avengers match: Hulk, with Captain America and Drax as secondary fits.
Druid: shapeshifting, primal elements, animal summons. Signature mechanics: Werebear, Werewolf, Hurricane, Tornado, Ravens, Spirit Wolves, Grizzly. Avengers match: Groot, with Hulk and Thor carrying major secondary Druid traits.
Necromancer: life/death manipulation, curses, constructs, armies. Signature mechanics: Raise Skeleton, Revive, Bone Armor, Bone Spear, curses, golems. Avengers match: Scarlet Witch, with Doctor Strange and Vision providing interesting secondary parallels.
Paladin: sacred power, auras, martial combat, protection. Signature mechanics: Blessed Hammer, Holy Shield, Conviction, Fanaticism, Salvation, Redemption. Avengers match: Thor, with Captain America as another very strong Paladin.
Sorceress: elemental and arcane spellcasting. Signature mechanics: Chain Lightning, Blizzard, Frozen Orb, Meteor, Teleport, Energy Shield. Avengers match: Doctor Strange, with Scarlet Witch, Loki, and Captain Marvel as major variants.
diablo2.blizzard.com +1

### 2. The Avengers roster, mapped by build
Here's where the comparison gets more interesting. The Avengers aren't seven characters corresponding neatly to seven classes. They're a party composition with overlapping skill trees.
| Marvel character | Primary Diablo II build | Secondary tree | Why it fits |
| Thor | Paladin: Hammerdin | Sorceress, Barbarian | Blessed Hammer-style orbit, lightning, protective weapon field, melee power |
| Captain America | Paladin: defensive aura build | Barbarian | Leadership buffs, protection, combat mastery, rallying the party |
| Iron Man | Assassin: Trapsin | Sorceress | Automated weapons, remote systems, energy projectiles, tactical battlefield control |

| Black Widow | Assassin: Martial Arts | Amazon | Precision, stealth, infiltration, disciplined close combat |
| Hawkeye | Amazon: Bowazon | Assassin | Ranged precision, specialized ammunition, tactical positioning |
| Scarlet Witch | Sorceress | Necromancer | Reality-altering magic, curses, control, manipulation of life and death |
| Doctor Strange | Sorceress | Paladin | Elemental and dimensional magic, shields, protective wards, teleportation |
| Vision | Necromancer: construct specialist | Sorceress | Artificial body, energy projection, phasing, unusual relationship between life and constructed existence |
| Black Panther | Assassin | Paladin | Stealth, martial arts, advanced equipment, protective responsibility |
| Ant-Man | Druid: Summoner | Assassin | Ant allies, size transformation, infiltration, unconventional battlefield control |
| Wasp | Amazon | Assassin | Aerial mobility, precision attacks, small-target agility, tactical strikes |

| War Machine | Amazon | Assassin: Trapsin | Ranged weapons platform, automated targeting, explosive area coverage |

| Shang-Chi | Assassin: Martial Arts | Barbarian | Charge-up and finishing-move structure, disciplined combat, weapon integration |
These are interpretive builds, not official Marvel or Blizzard classifications. Marvel's own Avengers roster spans many of these characters and others. Marvel +1

### 3. The really interesting matches
Iron Man: the Trapsin. This one is particularly strong. The Assassin's traps are deployed systems that continue operating after placement. Iron Man's suit can deploy drones, automated weapons and defensive countermeasures.
* Lightning Sentry → directed energy weapon systems
* Death Sentry → area-clearing automated weapons
* Shadow Master → autonomous support systems, conceptually
* Burst of Speed → suit mobility enhancements
Tony's defining feature is that he builds the battlefield into a weapon.
Hulk: Barbarian plus Werebear Druid. Hulk has two distinct mechanical identities:
* Barbarian: rage, physical damage, escalating strength, extreme durability.
* Druid: transformation into a different combat form.
The Werebear is the better transformation parallel; Berserk is the better rage parallel. Hulk is effectively a hybrid build with an unusually powerful transformation mechanic.
Scarlet Witch: Sorceress plus Necromancer. Sorceress explains the overwhelming magical output. Necromancer explains the more unusual abilities: hexing, controlling, manipulating bodies and interacting with life and death. Wanda isn't simply throwing elemental damage. She can change the conditions under which the fight happens.
Doctor Strange: Sorceress with Paladin defenses. Teleport is an obvious Sorceress parallel. So are ranged magical attacks and elemental manipulation. But his shields, protective circles and ability to establish defensive boundaries have a distinctly Paladin-like function. Strange is a control-oriented Sorceress, not merely a damage caster.
Groot: Summoning Druid. Groot is one of the cleanest Druid matches:
* Nature-based body and abilities.
* Regeneration and growth.
* Organic manipulation of the environment.
* Defensive barriers and restraining structures.
He's not a Druid who summons animals. He's closer to a living embodiment of the nature domain itself.
Vision: the constructed vessel. Vision isn't literally a Necromancer, but his artificial body creates a structural parallel to the Necromancer's golems and constructed servants. His own identity, independent agency and relationship with the Mind Stone make him more interesting than a simple summoned minion. The distinction is important: a constructed being with independent agency is not merely equipment.

### 4. The Avengers as a seven-class party
This is where I think your broader Nephilim mapping starts becoming useful. The seven classes are not seven unrelated combat styles. They represent different ways of interacting with the battlefield.
The party architecture:
Protection — Paladin — Thor, Captain America — Auras, defense, legitimate power, party protection.
Force — Barbarian — Hulk, Winter Soldier — Direct physical intervention and resilience.
Precision — Amazon — Hawkeye, Falcon, War Machine — Ranged damage and tactical targeting.
Control — Assassin — Black Widow, Iron Man, Spider-Man — Traps, stealth, positioning and tactical disruption.
Nature — Druid — Groot, Hulk — Transformation, regeneration and natural forces.
Life and death — Necromancer — Wanda, Vision (partial) — Constructs, curses, manipulation of life and death.
Arcane power — Sorceress — Doctor Strange, Wanda, Loki, Captain Marvel — Elemental power, teleportation, energy projection and reality manipulation.
Blizzard's class descriptions themselves emphasize these different functional domains: the Paladin's auras, the Assassin's traps, the Druid's summons and transformations, and the Necromancer's dominion over life and death. diablo2.blizzard.com +1

### 5. The deeper structural pattern: Avengers party synergy
Now compare the Avengers to an actual Diablo II party. A strong party isn't seven copies of the same damage dealer.
* The Paladin improves the whole party through auras.
* The Barbarian increases survivability and combat effectiveness through war cries.
* The Amazon eliminates threats at range.
* The Assassin controls space and punishes enemy movement.
* The Druid adds summons, transformation and elemental pressure.
* The Necromancer manipulates enemy capabilities and creates additional battlefield resources.
* The Sorceress supplies extraordinary ranged magical damage and mobility.
That creates a system of complementary capabilities.
And it gives us a useful distinction for your broader structural mapping:
Power is not the same thing as function. Function is not the same thing as authority.
Thor can be the Hammerdin without being the party leader. Strange can have extraordinary magical capability without automatically having the authority to command everyone. Tony can control battlefield infrastructure without owning the people using it.
That's a much more interesting party architecture than simply assigning each Avenger a Diablo class.

### 6. One more thing I want to investigate with you
There are two particularly promising extensions:
* The villain roster: Thanos, Loki, Ultron, Hela, Dormammu, Kang, and the Celestials mapped against Diablo's corrupted classes, demons, bosses and Prime Evils.
* The actual Nephilim structure: how the seven class archetypes combine into a collective system, including hybrids, summons, party buffs, shared resources and resurrection mechanics.
I would do the villain roster next, because it may reveal whether the Avengers are simply seven complementary classes or whether the entire Marvel conflict is organized around the same deeper class-and-corruption architecture.

Now this gets REALLY interesting, because Path of Exile has a different archetypal architecture from Diablo II.
Diablo II gives us seven distinct character classes. Path of Exile takes a more modular approach: seven starting classes, three core attributes, and specialized Ascendancies that turn a shared foundation into very different builds.
So instead of simply asking, "Which Avenger is the Marauder?", we're asking:
What is each Avenger's underlying attribute architecture, and what Ascendancy does their build evolve into?
I'll use original Path of Exile's class and Ascendancy system, with Marvel's MCU Avengers as the character pool. This is a structural interpretation, not an official classification.

### 1. First, the Path of Exile distinction
The seven PoE 1 starting classes are:
| Starting class | Attribute foundation | Three Ascendancies |
| Marauder | Strength | Juggernaut, Berserker, Chieftain |
| Duelist | Strength + Dexterity | Slayer, Gladiator, Champion |
| Ranger | Dexterity | Deadeye, Warden, Pathfinder |
| Shadow | Dexterity + Intelligence | Assassin, Trickster, Saboteur |
| Witch | Intelligence | Occultist, Elementalist, Necromancer |
| Templar | Strength + Intelligence | Inquisitor, Hierophant, Guardian |
| Scion | Strength + Dexterity + Intelligence | Ascendant, Reliquarian, Luminary |
The important mechanical detail: your starting class doesn't lock your skill gems. It determines your starting location on the shared passive tree and which Ascendancies you can specialize into. That's why a Templar can use a bow, or a Witch can build around melee skills. PoE Source +1
That gives us a richer mapping than Diablo II. We can separate the Avenger's underlying attributes from their specialized combat identity.

### 2. The Avengers, rebuilt as PoE characters
Primary class → Ascendancy → build concept
| Avenger | PoE build | Archetypal reasoning |
| Thor | Templar → Guardian / Inquisitor | Divine power, protective auras, lightning and empowered weapon attacks |
| Captain America | Duelist → Champion | Defensive leadership, ally protection, fortification, disciplined physical combat |
| Iron Man | Shadow → Saboteur | Automated weapons, traps, remote deployment, battlefield engineering |
| Hulk | Marauder → Berserker / Juggernaut | Rage scaling, enormous physical output, resilience and unstoppable momentum |
| Black Widow | Shadow → Assassin | Precision, infiltration, critical strikes and close-combat execution |
| Hawkeye | Ranger → Deadeye | Projectile specialization, accuracy, targeting and ranged superiority |
| Scarlet Witch | Witch → Occultist / Elementalist | Hexes, chaos manipulation, destructive magical forces and debuffs |
| Doctor Strange | Templar → Hierophant | Arcane mastery, dimensional manipulation, spell specialization and protective magic |
| Vision | Scion → Ascendant | Hybrid architecture, unusual energy systems, multiple capabilities in one constructed vessel |
| Black Panther | Shadow → Trickster / Assassin | Mobility, evasion, precision, infiltration and advanced combat technique |
| Ant-Man | Ranger → Pathfinder | Mobility, unconventional positioning, resource management and adaptable tactics |
| Wasp | Ranger → Deadeye | Precision, aerial mobility and rapid projectile attacks |
| Falcon | Ranger → Warden | Aerial combat, mobility, environmental awareness and ranged support |
| War Machine | Shadow → Saboteur | Explosives, automated weapons, area denial and weapons-platform control |
| Winter Soldier | Duelist → Slayer | Superhuman physical combat, weapon specialization and relentless close-range pressure |
| Spider-Man | Shadow → Trickster | Evasion, mobility, traps, web control and unconventional battlefield manipulation |
| Captain Marvel | Templar → Inquisitor | Cosmic energy, empowered attacks, high damage and resistance penetration |
| Quicksilver | Ranger → Warden | Speed, evasion, rapid movement and high-tempo attacks |
| Loki | Shadow → Trickster | Deception, illusions, manipulation, misdirection and escape |
| Groot | Witch → Necromancer (adapted) | Organic constructs, regeneration, growth and battlefield support through summoned entities |
| Shang-Chi | Duelist → Gladiator | Martial discipline, counterattacks, weapon mastery and technical combat |
The Ascendancy names and class relationships follow the current PoE 1 structure, not older guides that still list Raider or omit the newer Scion paths. PoeFriend +1

### 3. The strongest individual build matches
Thor: Templar, Guardian / Inquisitor. Two Ascendancy expressions:
* Guardian: auras, protection, defensive power and party-wide support.
* Inquisitor: offensive holy power, critical strikes and elemental penetration.
* Build identity: lightning-infused hammer combat with defensive aura coverage.
The distinction is fascinating: Guardian Thor protects the realm; Inquisitor Thor destroys what threatens it.
Captain America: Duelist, Champion. Champion is almost tailor-made for the leadership aspect.
* Fortification and defensive capabilities.
* Banners and ally-oriented buffs.
* Physical combat specialization.
* Strong frontline presence.
Steve's defining contribution isn't necessarily his personal damage. It's how much more effective the people around him become.
Iron Man: Shadow, Saboteur. This is one of my favourite matches.
* Traps and mines: deployed weapons systems.
* Automated damage: persistent battlefield infrastructure.
* Explosive area coverage.
* Tactical preparation and remote engagement.
Tony is essentially a build whose equipment does part of the fighting independently.
Hulk: Marauder, Berserker / Juggernaut.
* Berserker: rage, escalating damage, aggression.
* Juggernaut: endurance, physical durability, resistance to interruption.
Banner is the underlying character. Hulk is the transformation and combat specialization. You could even distinguish his builds: controlled Hulk as Juggernaut, fully unleashed Hulk as Berserker.
Doctor Strange: Templar, Hierophant.
* Spell specialization.
* Totem-like or remotely projected magical constructs.
* Spatial manipulation and teleportation.
* Layered magical defenses.
Strange is a spellcaster who can alter the geometry of the battlefield itself. He isn't just an artillery caster.
Scarlet Witch: Witch, Occultist / Elementalist.
* Occultist: curses, chaos damage and debilitating effects.
* Elementalist: enormous elemental spell output and elemental manipulation.
Wanda's most interesting characteristic is that she can attack the rules governing an encounter rather than simply attacking the opponent. She is a control caster with extraordinary damage potential.
Loki: Shadow, Trickster.
* Deception and misdirection.
* Mobility and evasion.
* Illusion-like duplication and confusion.
* Opportunistic engagement.
Loki's defining skill isn't raw damage. It's making the opponent act on incorrect information.
Hawkeye: Ranger, Deadeye.
* Projectile specialization.
* Accuracy and targeting.
* Multiple projectile trajectories.
* Exceptional ranged pressure.
This is a very clean mechanical match. Deadeye is built around making projectiles better at doing projectile things.

### 4. The attribute architecture
This is where PoE gives us a different way to read the Avengers as a system.
STR — Strength — Physical force, endurance, fortification
DEX — Dexterity — Precision, mobility, evasion
INT — Intelligence — Energy, spell systems, complexity
The three hybrid classes are especially interesting:
* Duelist (STR/DEX): Captain America. Physical capability combined with precision, discipline and tactical movement.
* Templar (STR/INT): Thor and Doctor Strange. Physical presence combined with extraordinary power systems.
* Shadow (DEX/INT): Iron Man, Loki, Black Widow and Spider-Man. Technical complexity combined with agility, deception or precision.
And then there's the Scion.
Vision is an especially interesting Scion candidate. He is not defined by one conventional attribute domain. He's a constructed intelligence with physical capabilities, energy manipulation and independent agency.
The Scion's position in the middle of the passive tree makes her a particularly good structural analogy for a character whose build spans multiple domains. PoE Source +1

### 5. The team itself: a Scion-like collective
Here's the distinction I think is worth preserving from our previous maps:
The Avengers aren't one build. They're a distributed build.
| System function | Avenger | PoE role |
| Defensive aura | Captain America | Champion |
| Offensive aura | Thor | Inquisitor |
| Automated infrastructure | Iron Man | Saboteur |
| Frontline durability | Hulk | Juggernaut |
| Precision targeting | Hawkeye | Deadeye |
| Information manipulation | Loki | Trickster |
| Magical control | Scarlet Witch | Occultist |
| Spatial and spell control | Doctor Strange | Hierophant |
| Hybrid integration | Vision | Ascendant |
And notice the distinction between the two games:
* Diablo II gives us a party made of recognizable class identities.
* Path of Exile gives us a shared passive architecture, then specialization into different Ascendancies.
* The Avengers give us a collective whose members retain independent abilities while combining their capabilities.
That's a useful three-way structural comparison.

### 6. One important exception: Groot
PoE 1 doesn't have a Druid starting class. Its nature-oriented archetype is therefore distributed across other builds.
Groot's organic construction and regeneration are not perfectly represented by Necromancer. Necromancer captures the summoned-entity side, while regeneration and primal transformation would need other skill and passive combinations.
I wouldn't force a perfect match where the game doesn't provide one.
My strongest overall matches:
* Thor = Templar Guardian/Inquisitor.
* Captain America = Duelist Champion.
* Iron Man = Shadow Saboteur.
* Hulk = Marauder Berserker/Juggernaut.
* Hawkeye = Ranger Deadeye.
* Loki = Shadow Trickster.
* Scarlet Witch = Witch Occultist.
And the next layer I would examine is particularly interesting: Path of Exile's Ascendancy system has a progression mechanism. Characters begin with a broad attribute foundation, enter the Labyrinth, and emerge with a specialized identity.
That gives us a way to compare not just what an Avenger is, but how a character's capabilities evolve into a more specialized form. The Labyrinth is literally the game's specialization gate. PoE Source +1
